Squid & Chickpea Marqa

Tunisian · Easy · Serves 4

The squid-and-chickpea marqa is the Tunisian coast's own thrift argument: the sea's cheap cephalopod and the pantry's cheapest legume, simmered long together in a tomato-harissa pot until the squid turns butter-tender and the chickpeas have drunk the pot's red. The doctrine is the sea-meets-pantry braise that runs the whole Mediterranean's working kitchens — and the Tunisian register runs the fiercest pot on the row.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

  • a 30-minute pot's honest bridge)
- **Cook the squid long, not fast — the braise's own clock.** The squid's two clocks are the canon's great either-or: the fast fry's 90 seconds (#5's law) or the long braise's 45-plus minutes — and this pot runs the long road, the squid's collagen melting to butter through the slow simmer. The in-between (the 10-minute pot) is the rubber road, and it has no travelers worth feeding. - **The bridge:** the frozen cleaned squid runs truly (thawed, dried); the canned chickpea cuts the pot to 30 honest minutes (add them with the squid — their drinking's clock is done).

Squid & Chickpea Marqa

Prep: 20 minutes, plus 8 hours soaking · Cook: 1 hour 20 minutes · Total: About 9 hours 45 minutes (mostly soaking) · Serves 4

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 600 g squid, cleaned, bodies cut to rings and tentacles halved (about 500 g cleaned)
  • 200 g dried chickpeas, soaked 8 hours (or 400 g canned, drained — a 30-minute pot's honest bridge)
  • 3 tbsp olive oil (about 40 g); 1 onion (about 150 g), sliced
  • 5 cloves garlic (about 20 g), sliced; 1 tbsp tomato paste (about 15 g)
  • 2 tbsp harissa (#91 — the pot's own fire) or 1 tbsp plus chile flakes
  • 1 tsp cumin; 1 tsp caraway (the Tunisian note); 1 tsp salt
  • 500 g tomatoes, grated, or 1 can crushed; 400 ml water (about 400 g)
  • A fist of cilantro (about 15 g), half tied, half at the end; the juice of ½ a lemon
  • To serve: bread (about 300 g), the #116 cumin salt, and more harissa at the dial

Instructions

  1. **The base (10 minutes).** Warm the oil; soften the onion 5 minutes; the garlic, the tomato paste, the harissa, and the spices fried 2 minutes to the pot's fierce perfume — the harissa's bloom in oil is the whole kitchen's register. Checkpoint — the paste darkened, the oil run red-orange at the pot's edges — the Tunisian pot's own beginning, and the harissa's raw edge cooked to its depth.
  2. **The long braise (1 hour at the tremble).** The tomatoes, the water, the soaked chickpeas, the tied herbs, and the salt in — brought to a bare simmer, covered, and trembled (95 °C) 30 minutes (the chickpeas' head start). The squid stirred in; covered again, and trembled 45 minutes more, until the chickpeas are fully tender and the squid yields to the spoon's edge. Checkpoint — the squid's test: a ring's bite — butter-tender, no resistance, no rubber (the long clock's own proof). The chickpeas: tender to their centers, their flavor run through with the pot's red. The sauce: thick, tomato-harissa deep, coat-the-spoon. If the squid still fights at 45, ten more minutes at the tremble is its mercy.
  3. **The finish and the table.** Off the flame: the lemon's juice, the fresh cilantro, a thread of raw olive oil — the rest 5 minutes, and the pot served with bread and the cumin salt. Checkpoint — eating test, with bread: the squid's butter-tender chew and the chickpeas' earth in the same spoonful — the pot's red fire (the harissa's warmth) running through both, the lemon's cut at the swallow — the bread sopping the deepest red. It should taste like the coast's thrift at its finest: the two cheapest things in the market, and a pot better than the sum of either.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Squid rubberyThe middle road's clockThe long braise \u2014 45 minutes minimum
Pot one-note fierceHarissa run without its bloomThe 2-minute fry in oil first
Chickpeas hard at the potUnder-soaked or under-trembledThe full soak; the full clock

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- Keeps 3 days refrigerated and improves (the squid steeping to its finest); the reheat is a gentle covered simmer. The canned-chickpea version runs 30 minutes to the day's pot. - Variations: the octopus's longer clock, the shrimp's last-5-minutes register. The #91 harissa is this pot's own parent; the #2 koshari's row is the legume canon's Egypt seat.
